entries.summary: Sprint reset: today is Day 0 and the gate review moves from 13 Jan 2027 to 1 Dec 2026
details: The sprint is now 42 days, not 90. Checkpoints fall on Day 5 (25 Oct), Day 19 (8 Nov) and Day 33 (22 Nov), with the gate on Day 42.

Standards tightened: hard timers of 20, 35 and 50 minutes; any hinted or failed problem is re-solved cold within 48 hours and again after 7 days; an overdue retest blocks new material; a failed checkpoint freezes new topics in that area.
Each status now has a written evidence threshold (see Roadmap). Previous statuses are unchanged because none had been re-tested.
Retest deadlines were reset: the four Week 0 retests are due 20 to 22 Oct, the unseen sliding-window set 25 Oct. The earlier 18 Oct deadline passed with no submission logged.
Behavioral stories now start in Week 1 because leadership principles come up in every Amazon round, and low-level design is brought forward ahead of deep system design.
Cut from the old plan: 2D DP and knapsack, tries, shortest paths and MST, the voice agent trace, replication and CAP depth, the publishable queue project and a second resume pass.
No status changed and no new evidence was added.

entries.summary: Day 1 of the 90-day sprint; roadmap compressed to v2.2
details: Sprint runs 2026-10-16 to the 2027-01-13 gate review.
Week 0 tasks (Lesson 1 A to C, the route trace, the LC 643 and LC 209 retests) were not submitted as of 18:28.
Request lifecycle: browser events only, with no DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP or server path (W-004).
Methods and status codes: weak. 401 vs 403 confused; PUT and PATCH blank.
Indexes: knew B-tree and separate storage; write cost and the case where an index does not help were blank.
Last-seat booking race answered as a deadlock; it is a lost-update race (W-005).
SQL vs Mongo: data shape only, no trade-offs.
Worker crash: knew job state must be durable; missed acknowledgement, redelivery and idempotency (W-006).
Blank: retries, caching, thread race, GIL, API design, explaining the job worker (W-007).
Result: baseline set. Databases, networking, distributed systems and system design stay NOT STARTED; operating systems stays LEARNING.
